hints.text: A test that `return`s early passes silently: `ok N` in ~1 ms, `# skipped 0`. Gate with test(name, { skip: cond ? reason : false }) so TAP prints `# SKIP <reason>`, and prove the skip by running the file in a scratch copy.

A mutation generator must continue past a cut test file (UNDECIDED only if nothing killed it and one file was cut) and pass --test-force-exit: one leaked listener otherwise leaves a mutant undecided and blocks the END state.

A pins file that pins the GREEN manifest makes the GREEN come first. Run that one GREEN with an env switch (C017_END_STATE=run) so the END-state tests execute for real, then write pins.json LAST and run the plain suite.

Count, do not time, a leak: expose a read-only accessor (size of the tracked set) and assert on server-side socket `close` events; Node server.close(cb) fires before the sockets own close events, so wait for them first.

Windows: node --test rejects an absolute --test-reporter path; pass a relative path or a file: URL. A wrapper reporter that replaces repo root, home and user name keeps identifiers out of archived transcripts.

heavy-slot.ps1 Release frees EVERY lock whose content starts with "<owner> ": give each parallel driver its own owner name, and touch the lock mtime during runs (a holder silent for 60 minutes is reclaimed).
PowerShell variables are case-insensitive: `foreach ($name ...)` overwrote `param($Name)`, so a driver wrote its status lines to files named after the loop items. Use distinct variable names.

Per-file 85/85/85 with the 43 fast test files is enough when the child-process, attacker and evidence tests are left out and NAMED; assert the left-out list from the capture command so the README cannot drift.

To close F24 for many connections feed the parser slices of ~2 KB from a hand-installed data listener (keep Node socket._paused intact): one 64 KB read costs 2.4 to 6.5 MB, times 64 connections about 416 MB.

obstacles.what: F24 is not closed for many connections: the bound is one 64 KB socket read per connection and Node parser builds a request and response for every request of that read before any handler runs, so 32 connections of 50-byte requests (8 of 18-byte ones, 64 of either) still abort a 48 MB-heap child (exit 134); a default heap holds the worst case (about 416 MB).
obstacles.removedBy: A fix of server.cjs that bounds the parse work per read (a hand-installed data listener feeding the parser slices of about 2 KB and stopping at the first destroyed socket, keeping Node socket._paused handling), written test-first with a many-connection process test (32 connections of the 18-byte request in a 48 MB child) and followed by a recapture of every capture because each pins server.cjs.

Ran the recorded campaign at Normal priority, 4 workers, inside my own heavy-slot window (rule 13 says BelowNormal): 351 mutants took 389 s at Normal and 62 minutes at BelowNormal; the BelowNormal result was undecided.

archive-run manifests cannot be repaired: any manifest with a wrong exit code or a stale input pin fails evidence.test forever. Run once unrecorded (a dry browser run, --limit/--only campaigns), keep pinned input lists narrow, move failed captures out before publishing.

mutants.cjs --live <file> tees stderr (survivors, progress) while the shared recorder, which writes transcripts only at the end, is running; --only <ids> reruns exact mutants; --limit 0 runs only the baseline of the unmutated suites.

A flood or resource test that asserts a duration (flood 12 s, lag 4 s, GET 6 s, keep-alive 3 s) fails on a busy machine: decide on closed sockets, answered probes, collected heap, bytes read per refused connection and the server's configured timers; keep only hang detectors.

A mutation driver must treat a suite timeout as UNDECIDED, never as a kill: 4 of 45 recorded kills had no named failing test (the mutant hung the suite). Run campaigns at NORMAL priority with at most 4 workers and a generous timeout; BelowNormal gets 2 to 4 percent of a core on this machine (controller correction to rule 13).

Publish order that worked: freeze, then the no-slot captures (mutants, green) and the slot captures (coverage, browser) in parallel, evidence-02 last (it took 579 s on a busy machine: it spawns git cat-file for every sealed pin). A transient nested exit 1 of the server.cjs coverage command (333 of 333 passed, no coverage row) was retained as evidence\raw\failed-attempt-coverage-02-1 and the capture repeated.

RED for a load flake: a --require preload that busy-waits 5 s in the server child at its first connection (a correct server the scheduler did not run); the old test fails on its lag and keep-alive bounds, the new one passes, and the lag the child measured proves the stall.

Without a 'connect' listener Node destroys a CONNECT socket at once: a valid mutation written before the CONNECT in one write applies and its answer is lost. Answer the CONNECT through the parse-error path after the earlier answers (405 with Allow); an Upgrade header needs no listener (ignored, ordinary request).

Measure the bytes the server READ from a refused connection (socket.bytesRead at close, reported by the child): a correct server reads one 64 KB chunk (65,648 at most), a server that does not destroy after the flush reads 2 MB; this kills the mutant structurally instead of by lag.

A generic aliasing walker found three exported plain arrays (validate.STEP_KEYS, envelope.ENVELOPE_KEYS, verify.REQUIRED_CODES) in UMD validators; export frozen copies. Do not walk prototypes or functions: the first version overwrote Object.create and Object.freeze.

No 'upgrade' listener: Node serves an Upgrade request as an ordinary one without a listener (RFC 9110 allows ignoring it), so the closing mark in handle() applies; a listener would be a second entrance that bypasses the handler. Rows for websocket and h2c in both framings prove it.

A RED manifest pins its inputs: editing a pinned helper (pipe-support.cjs) after archiving invalidates the RED. Re-archive the REDs whose inputs changed (cheap: seconds) before the captures, and never edit a pinned input afterwards.

Generated mutation campaign: node tests\mutgen.cjs --lines=a-b,c-d --parallel=4 (position-based mutants through tests\mutate-at.cjs, staged suites, survivors need tests\mutgen-equivalent.json). On a busy machine a survivor costs about 1 minute, so 269 mutants of server.cjs need more than an hour: run it early, on a quiet machine, before freezing.

A mutation preload that exits 99 when it applied nothing also fires in the node --test runner process, which never loads the target: every suite looked like a survivor. Decide application inside the process that loads the file, or not at all.

Fresh checkout: a local clone without checkout outside the repository, git archive HEAD of the imports (LF), working namespace overlaid, optional CRLF conversion; the evidence and replay suites need the captures, so run those last or exclude them and say so.

No 'upgrade' listener: Node serves an Upgrade request as an ordinary one without a listener (RFC 9110 allows ignoring it), so the closing mark in handle() applies; a listener would be a second entrance that bypasses the handler. Rows for websocket and h2c in both framings prove it.

A RED manifest pins its inputs: editing a pinned helper (pipe-support.cjs) after archiving invalidates the RED. Re-archive the REDs whose inputs changed (cheap: seconds) before the captures, and never edit a pinned input afterwards.

Generated mutation campaign: node tests\mutgen.cjs --lines=a-b,c-d --parallel=4 (position-based mutants through tests\mutate-at.cjs, staged suites, survivors need tests\mutgen-equivalent.json). On a busy machine a survivor costs about 1 minute, so 269 mutants of server.cjs need more than an hour: run it early, on a quiet machine, before freezing.

A mutation preload that exits 99 when it applied nothing also fires in the node --test runner process, which never loads the target: every suite looked like a survivor. Decide application inside the process that loads the file, or not at all.

Fresh checkout: a local clone without checkout outside the repository, git archive HEAD of the imports (LF), working namespace overlaid, optional CRLF conversion; the evidence and replay suites need the captures, so run those last or exclude them and say so.

rev-C059 N1 (third pipelining hole): with two or three legitimate requests before a Node-own refusal ([G][G][X], [G][G][G][X], [G][G][X][G], [POST][G][X]) C043 answers them in order, then the typed 417/421/400/431, then closes; 128 sockets of [G][G][X] do not pin the cap. Because checkExpectation and clientError use the same per-connection lane, the probe passed first time.

Per-file 85/85/85 held on the 11 production files after the R3 changes; the server.cjs command now also loads the connect-upgrade, two-instances and boundaries suites (more suites can only raise a figure). The first coverage-02 capture failed once on server.cjs only (nested exit 1, 333 of 333 tests passed, no coverage row) and a direct rerun gave 98.24 / 96.89 / 91.49: it is retained as evidence\raw\failed-attempt-coverage-02-1 and the capture was repeated.

rules.name: Atomic
rules.text: One card is one owner, one behavior, one reviewable change set, one observable check and one to four focused hours. Split decisions, hidden builds and oversize cards before pulling.

rules.name: Kano
rules.text: Every credit-bearing card has one frozen class. Unblock, slice, tooling and quality-debt work is zero credit and never funds a quota.

rules.name: No Blocked
rules.text: Only To Do, In Progress and Done exist. An obstacle becomes a U card in the same transaction and is pulled first; the stopped card returns to To Do gated on it.

rules.name: TDD
rules.text: Specification, a genuine archived RED, GREEN, refactor, for every card type.

rules.name: 85% coverage
rules.text: At least 85% line, branch and function coverage per production file over the enumerated file set; unloaded files count as 0%; no waivers.

rules.name: Parallel by design
rules.text: One namespace per card, single-writer shared files, narrow gates, To Do filled widest-first, frontier measured at each replenishment.

rules.name: Shared memory
rules.text: Read lessons and hints before planning or pulling; leave hints when finishing, stopping or refining.

lessons.text: Publish only via .git\kanban-orchestrator\publish.ps1. A manual 'git add --all' commit (dd49966d) put five in-progress cards' unpublished files into one unscoped commit and skipped their card-scoped tags.
A nested 'node --test' started inside a test inherits NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8 and exits 0 even when its test fails. Spawn it with NODE_TEST_CONTEXT and NODE_V8_COVERAGE deleted from the child env.
Node coverage reports only files a test loads and counts no branches inside uncalled functions. Enumerate production files and count unloaded ones as 0% before trusting any percentage.
node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-coverage-include=<file> --test-coverage-lines=85 --test-coverage-branches=85 --test-coverage-functions=85 <tests>; exits 1 below any threshold.
Staged CRLF files: git -c core.whitespace=blank-at-eol,blank-at-eof,space-before-tab,cr-at-eol diff --cached --check. Plain 'git diff --check' flags every CRLF line as trailing whitespace.

Ledger writes hold mutex Local\AppScalingStrategies_KanbanState_v1. The ledger is CRLF; ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 60 reproduces it byte for byte, Node JSON.stringify does not.
A card is publishable only after its exact ID and frozen Kano class are in publish.ps1's closed map (A-Snnn are pattern-allowed). Admit the publication scope before admitting the card.
Admin publication (publish.ps1 -Admin) accepts only .docs\wiki\flow-state.json and .docs\wiki\kanban.md with a [flow][admin] message; any other path needs an owned card scope.
Consumers pin accepted producer bytes and sealed evidence is hash-checked. Quality-debt work adds test files only; editing production source or sealed files breaks pins and integrity tests.

Browser checks: require('./testing/browser/isolated.cjs').openIsolatedLesson(relPath) starts fresh headless Edge for files under learning/, capability/ or testing/browser/fixtures/; always await session.close() in finally.
Set CAPTURE_BROWSER_EVIDENCE=1 only for an intentional evidence refresh; ordinary verification must leave every evidence byte unchanged.
If git push fails with a server error, retry with command-local 'git -c http.version=HTTP/1.1 push'; never change global git or TLS settings.
Native cards C061-C108 hide adapter plumbing (ARM auth, lease-scoped tags, idempotent operations, error mapping). Before admission, split an offline recorded-response slice from the native-run slice.
The dependency graph is narrow at the start: depth 11, six unstarted ready C cards, and SAFE (C056) at depth 6 gating every native and B card. Keep agents busy with independent U and K work.

All five In Progress claims show no change under their namespaces since 12:10-12:14Z (07:10-07:14 local) while the ledger still says running. Re-attach a fresh agent to the same worker ID with state.ps1 -Action AgentId: card publication wrappers hard-code worker IDs, so returning the card to To Do would strand its publication.

Tests that compare an installed browser version or SHA to a recorded value fail on every routine Edge update. 57 namespaces hard-code Edge 156.0.4314.50 and the installed Edge is now 156.0.4314.58. Assert the signature and the qualified major version, and record the actual values.

Tests that read ambient mutable state fail when other agents work. C035's foreign-index test can never hold again after the unscoped commit, and C005, C015 and C034 pin an old publisher digest. Build the state in a fixture or pin an archived snapshot.

Card publication wrappers (capability/Cnnn/publish.ps1) require the card In Progress under a hard-coded worker ID with status running, plus the exact frozen kanban row. Changing any of them strands publication.

Accepted lessons pin exact spans of kanban.md by the first occurrence of a heading or sentence. Editing a pinned span, or quoting its opening words earlier in the file, failed 23 lesson integrity suites during this hygiene pass. See Pinned text.

The learning/S011 browser suite rewrites its committed evidence/browser-observations.json on every run (start time, finish time and Edge version changed); S009, S015, S112 and S123 write only under CAPTURE_BROWSER_EVIDENCE=1. After any local browser run, check git status and git restore evidence you did not mean to change.

Node prints no coverage row and exits 0 for a file no test loads (app.js was 0%). tests\coverage.cjs requires a row per enumerated file, so unloaded counts as 0%; run it directly or via verify.cjs coverage.

Browser-only app.js is covered under Node: fake document/Option globals, delete require.cache, require it, poll #status; stub crypto.subtle.digest to reach defense-in-depth branches. 24 tests give app.js 100/100/100.
