lessons.text: A confinement check that compares [IO.Path]::GetFullPath strings with the owned root is not enough, because git interprets the ORIGINAL arguments and the process working directory. Pathspec magic (:(exclude)x/../scope/f, :!, :^) makes git add and commit --only take every other modified or untracked file; 8.3 short names (CAPABI~1) are expanded by GetFullPath but stored literally by git; a non-root cwd shifts containment; case variants leave a stray staged entry. publish.ps1 has the same three holes (rev-U003 reproduced them). Fix: pass the global option git --literal-pathspecs (not the environment variable, which leaks into the caller shell), whitelist path segments, require cwd equal to rev-parse --show-toplevel, compare the namespace prefix ordinally and re-check the staged paths after git add. Until a hardened publisher exists, pass only plain relative paths from the repository root.
lessons.evidence: reviews/U003.verdict.json (blockers 1-3, reproduced in throwaway repos only)

lessons.text: An independent reviewer with an attack list found three blockers that the author 94 tests and 15 mutants missed: the author tried hostile input classes (pathspec magic) for only one ID family. For every guard test each hostile class against EVERY identity family, make the reviewer write its own probes, and send the fix back to the same reviewer for the re-review (it already knows the attacks) while a different agent writes the fix.

String.StartsWith is culture-sensitive: a soft hyphen or a zero-width space inside [C026]<U+00AD>[S] still matches and is committed. Use [StringComparison]::Ordinal for every identity, prefix and path comparison, and reject non-ASCII before the prefix ends. The same applies to -like and -match on identifiers.

A coordinator agent started with the task tool has no background mode: every spawn blocks it, so its waves stall behind the slowest or silent worker (run 2 hung behind w-C009). The parent agent should coordinate: launch workers and reviewers with mode background, receive completion notifications, read heartbeat files, and treat a heartbeat older than 40 minutes as a stall to reassign. Keep the machine under about 8 running agents and 3 heavy browser or coverage runs.

Amendment pattern for a sealed test (U020 on C034; precedents C030, C035, C036): a chained, append-only evidence-index-addendum-N.json with a closed AMENDABLE list; each entry is applied (bytes already replaced) or authorized (exact pre-approved future bytes with base path and hash). The replaced integrity test stays byte-identical under evidence and is superseded by addendum 1. The new integrity test pins the helper (amendments.cjs) by raw SHA so the chain is acyclic; a later helper edit needs addendum 2. Test the hash logic with in-memory fixtures (a Map of path to Buffer) and pure functions.
lessons.evidence: capability/C034/U020.md; reviews/U020.verdict.json; precedents C030, C035, C036

lessons.text: A scratch copy of a namespace used for a RED or GREEN replay needs the namespaces it imports (C034 trace.js requires C020 and C033) and a git init (an unborn HEAD reads as pending); some tests also need C015, C001 and the live ledger. Replay only the integrity logic in scratch and run the other suites in the real tree.

A namespace's own integrity test cannot detect a CONSISTENT rewrite of the verifier plus its own addendum (probe D5: replacing integrity.test.cjs and the addendum sha passes all 15 tests); git history of the accepted commit is the only detector. Independent reviewers must diff every verifier file against the accepted commit and recompute the pinned hashes themselves.

A before/after dependency tripwire (hash the tree, run the verifier, hash again) detects only MID-RUN changes. Scoping it to a pinned list of accepted files (U021: 161 files in an append-only addendum) keeps mid-run modification and removal red and makes added files harmless; it never detects a STATIC edit of a listed file, which only a byte pin with an amendment path (C016 dependency-pins addenda, C034 seal addenda) can. Keep both kinds when you need both guarantees.

Replacing an enumerate-everything check by a pinned list silently drops implicit protections (link and junction detection, unlisted entries, parent directories). When you scope a check, list every protection the old form gave, document which ones are dropped on purpose, and restore the ones that matter test-first.

Agent sandboxes forbid %TEMP% scratch directories: workers and reviewers put scratch under RUN\scratch\<agent-or-item>\ with SHORT folder names (Windows MAX_PATH 259 breaks git show <rev>:<path> in deep scratch paths) and delete it at the end. Do not tell reviewers to use $env:TEMP.

Gate coverage with ONE L-0004 command per file: a single command with several --test-coverage-include values and the same thresholds checks only the aggregate row and hides a weak file. Archive one manifest per file (command, exit code, input SHA-256) so a reviewer can replay each.

K evidence layout that publishes cleanly: evidence/<item>/ with a .gitattributes of '* -text -diff', one manifest JSON per run (command, exit, input SHA-256, parsed counts) plus raw/*.raw.gz transcripts. Raw node --test coverage stdout has trailing spaces that fail the publisher's diff --cached --check, so archive transcripts gzip-compressed; manifests stay plain JSON. About 25 minutes per K item with this layout.

A UMD file with an untested browser-global branch gets covered by running the real source with new vm.Script(src, { filename: pathToFileURL(file).href }) in a fresh context without module or require (and, for page scripts, with the real dependency scripts in index.html order); Node merges that run with the require runs of the same file (plan-fixtures.js branches 70 to 100). UMD wrappers define globals with non-writable, non-configurable properties: to omit or replace an authority, skip its script or pre-define the replacement on the vm context before the script runs; in a vm, delete of a non-configurable global returns false instead of throwing.

Pin the helper that an amendment-aware integrity test trusts: U020 pins amendments.cjs by raw SHA inside the integrity test (acyclic), U019 did not pin pin-authority.cjs, so a permissive stub passes the integrity test and only the spec tests notice. When you add an amendment path, pin the checker and say in the README how a later addendum interacts with the integrity test and when an authorized replacement becomes applied.

Archive every mutation script you cite with its list of mutants and the raw result: a reviewer can re-run an archived tool (K-C004: 20 of 20 re-killed) but can only trust a claimed 'N of N mutants killed' that is not archived (U019). Keep mutation scripts in scratch only if you also archive their output and the mutant diffs.

After a K pin edit the archived RED-01 and RED-02 no longer fail in place. Replay their reasons in a SCRATCH COPY of the namespace with the retained pre-edit file copied beside the edited one under a non-test name (for example tests\surface.before-k-c034.cjs), run it plain and under the no-live-publisher guard, and never in the repository.

A guard that monkey-patches fs to throw when a test touches a live file (the no-live-publisher fixture) is a tripwire, not a sandbox: junctions, hard links, 8.3 short names and copyFileSync bypass it. Say so in the README and keep the real protection in archived-snapshot assertions.

Before every publication run a pre-flight: no junction or symlink and no nested .git inside the namespace (git follows a junction and publishes outside content under the namespace path; a nested repo is committed as a gitlink), GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE unset in the shell, cwd equal to the repository root, git diff --cached --name-only empty, plain folder path or explicit files without a trailing backslash. Late failures after staging leave the requested paths staged: unstage them yourself and report.

pwsh -File passes an array argument such as -Paths a,b or -Ids 'K-C008','K-C004' as ONE string. Call scripts through pwsh -Command "& 'script.ps1' -Ids @('a','b')" or build the -Command string with @('a','b') literals. Also: $x = if (cond) { @($one) } else { @() } unrolls a one-element array into a bare object; assign the array before the if.

lessons.evidence: reviews/U019.verdict.json; reviews/U020.verdict.json; results/U019.json notes; results/U020.json hints
lessons.text: git ls-remote is a NETWORK call even when read-only; three workers and several reviewers slipped. Compare HEAD with the remote through git rev-parse origin/main (after the publisher's own fetch) and let the publisher do the remote verification; reviewers may run exactly one ls-remote for the tag.

Prove that observations are independent of an ambient channel such as cookies non-vacuously: run the same request sequence under several regimes (no cookie, a conflicting decoy cookie on every request, a jar fed by a foreign origin, regimes alternating request by request) and record at the SERVER what the channel actually carried; equality of the observations only means something when the server-side hook shows that the regimes really differed on the wire. Also assert the server never emits Set-Cookie and never reads the Cookie header.

A network parser must bound memory per CONNECTION, not only per message: zero-length continuation frames (a fragmented WebSocket message made of endless empty frames) were never counted against the 4096-byte limit and cost about 32 heap bytes per wire byte, and a client that sends pings and never reads grows the outbound queue without bound. Cap the number of fragments per message, the total buffered bytes and the outbound queue, and close with the protocol code (1009 too big). The same families apply to HTTP/2 and gRPC (empty DATA frames, CONTINUATION or header floods, zero-length messages) and to SSE slow readers.

closeServer must track and destroy EVERY accepted socket, including sockets refused at upgrade (the 426 path) and half-open ones: an untracked refused-upgrade socket kept closeServer pending for 36 s until the client closed. Track sockets from the connection event, end and destroy the refused socket after writing the response, and test shutdown with a half-open client (net.connect with allowHalfOpen) that never closes.

Resource-exhaustion defects are found by running the server in a child process under a small heap (node --max-old-space-size=96) with a hard external timeout and feeding crafted frames; turn each reproduction into a bounded automated test for every network-facing parser and server (WebSocket, SSE, gRPC) before asking for review.

To prove that unchanged or forged traffic CANNOT inflate a rate, enumerate: an exhaustive run over every trace of a small event alphabet (1,118,481 traces) plus a randomized mutation run (180,000) beats hand-picked cases and found no inflation path in C031. Assert the numerator only rises for legitimate transitions and no eligible client leaves the denominator, and make empty or degenerate input explicit (0 of 0 with a null percent, never NaN or 100%).

Do not derive eligibility from the FIRST versioned event: a replayed v2 request or state placed first removed stuck v1 clients from the denominator (3 of 8 became 3 of 5). Any old-version event keeps a client eligible; label the contradictory start (CONTRADICTORY_START_COUNTED_ELIGIBLE) and count it, so a denominator can only shrink through an explicit, visible rule.

Pins in imports.json are only as strong as their anchor: a forged bundle whose pins were re-signed in the same namespace passes the pin checks and is caught only by content expectations in the suite; the published tag or commit of the accepted producer is the real anchor, so recompute pins against git at the accepted commit, not against the file next to them.

Client duplicate-detection state must survive EVERY recovery path: reducer.resync() reset lastSeq and epoch to null, so replaying the server retained window after a typed CURSOR_EXPIRED displayed 35 already-applied events as new (droppedDuplicates stayed 0) and the marker still said the range was a gap. Keep the watermark across a same-epoch resync, reset it only when the epoch changes, record a gap only when the first delivered seq is greater than lastSeq + 1 and name the exact range, and expect the replayed window of a cursorless stream to overlap what was already applied.

A recovery-step assertion that only checks the count went UP (applied > before) cannot see a duplicate defect: C044 own green browser snapshot held 119 entries with 35 repeated ids. After every recovery action (reconnect, resync, retry, restart) assert that the ids in the rendered log are unique and that applied + duplicates + skipped equals what was delivered, and scan your own archived DOM snapshot for repeated ids before publishing.

The operation alphabet of a stateful property test must include the RECOVERY operations (typed failure, resync, rewound re-request, restart with a new epoch) and the invariant must be global (no id applied twice, counts reconcile) and checked after EVERY operation: the C044 tests asserted lastSeq null after resync and never fed an overlapping window, while the reviewer fuzz that combined a resync with a replayed window reached the defect at once.

After answering a request whose body you refuse to read (UNEXPECTED_BODY 400), send Connection: close and destroy the socket once the response is flushed: otherwise Node keeps parsing an endless Transfer-Encoding: chunked body of 1-byte chunks (5 connections stalled the event loop 3.5 s and a concurrent GET timed out) although the heap stays flat. Apply the same close-after-refusal rule to every refused request of an HTTP fixture.

A retained RED must fail for the missing behavior, not for an invalid test input: the C044 RED test 1 asked for cursor 5 outside a 4-event window and fails with 410 even against a correct implementation (8 of 9 RED assertions pass unchanged against the real code, 9 of 9 once the window is widened). After GREEN replay the RED file against the final code: every assertion should pass unchanged, and a RED that still fails needs its input corrected in a NEW retained RED.

A document that states facts about the repository must name the HEAD commit it describes and be re-checked against git log since its date before review: the U001 packet of 4 Nov said no deployable artifact and no teardown code exist, and the owner own commit f42f4e03 of 5 Nov (demo/, infra/, workflows, .azure/deployment-plan.md) made both statements false. Keep a State-of-the-repository section with the commit hash, and let a validator require it.

A destructive step needs its guards IN the step, not only in prose: az group create is idempotent, so a pre-existing group would be re-tagged and later deleted by az group delete --yes. Gate creation with az group exists printing false, pin the subscription on every az command (az account show equals the approved id), and require the expected name and tags (lease-id, lease-expires-utc) from az group show before each delete. The owner demo/cleanup.cjs already implements the three guards and is the model.

Cost ceilings are planning bounds, not Azure-enforced limits (budgets only alert and lag 8 to 24 hours). Compute the worst case with one teardown-latency hour at the instance cap, price list and create-container blob operations like writes, and label every spend ceiling planning bound; a worst case within one billed hour of a ceiling step is brittle (option C 70 flips to 75).

Quota is a price-like fact: a non-deploying ARM validation on 5 Nov was rejected with InternalSubscriptionIsOverQuotaForSku (P1v3 limit 0) in centralus, northcentralus, eastus2 and westus2. A packet or plan that offers a SKU and region must say whether quota was validated by a non-deploying validation or what-if in the owner subscription or is unproven, and a default option must not rest on a combination known to have failed.

Keep the self-check of a generated document as a runnable artifact: passed with 0 errors and 14 negative controls cannot be re-run when the script was inline and discarded. Turn review findings into permanent validator rules with negative fixtures (U001 validator under testing/quality), so the next packet is checked by code before an independent reviewer reads it.

A server fixture must cut slow-handshake and idle connections, not only silent ones: a first-byte timeout that is disabled on the first byte let 128 sockets that sent a preface prefix and idled exhaust maxConnections and lock out a legitimate client. Keep a handshake and idle timeout that the first byte does not disable, give drain() a bound or document that it needs abort() or close(),       and give calls an idle limit.

A guard implemented with a timer can make its own mutant HANG the suite instead of failing it, because node:test's default per-test timeout is Infinity: give every network or timer test an explicit timeout (test options or --test-timeout) so that removing a guard fails with a named assertion in seconds,       not a 150 s kill.

Inject a manual scheduler into servers, services and drivers (capability/C028/timers.cjs ManualTimers with whenPending): deadlines, pacing and cancel become exact without sleeps, wall-clock flakiness under load disappears and browser transcripts are reproducible byte for byte. Clamp timer delays above 2147483647 ms, which Node wraps to 1 ms.

Fixed-timeout verify wrappers (C016 900 s, C018 540 s, C019 600 s) fail with ETIMEDOUT and no assertion failure when concurrent heavy runs saturate the machine, and a killed run leaves test-<uuid> scratch namespaces that make C015 verify.cjs fail with Unclean owned scratch. Run such wrappers alone under a heavy slot, never read a timeout as a defect without a rerun on a quiet machine, and remove only the scratch you created.

A rejection-fix cycle that passes its re-review: the fix order maps every finding to a test-first RED archived in a NEW directory (the first publication's evidence stays immutable), the fix commit publishes once, new captures come last, and the SAME reviewer re-attacks with its own reproductions plus siblings of the class and re-runs its regression probes. The reviewer's best checks were replaying the RED both ways (first-publication bytes fail, final code passes unchanged) and mutating each fix in a private copy so that exactly the tests that name it die.

Apply close-after-refusal in the ONE central send path for EVERY refusal the server can produce, then test it over a table of all refusal statuses: C044 closed only the reported GET-with-body refusal, while 405, 421 and 403 answers with an endless chunked body still stalled the event loop 2.7 to 3.7 s. When a lesson names a class (refused requests keep parsing the body), fix the class and prove it with a table-driven test,       not only the reproduction.

Prove every claim that a test pins evidence by TAMPERING: C044's README said surface.test.cjs pins the retained RED and raw evidence, but it only checked two .gitattributes lines and six tamper edits in a scratch copy left 130 of 130 tests green, while C026's evidence.test.cjs recomputes every hash and detects them. Before writing the claim, edit a retained file in a scratch copy and show the named test fail.

To prove that failed and unknown rows can never disappear from a table view, enumerate the WHOLE view space (every sort column and direction x every status-filter subset x page sizes including 0, 1, negative and NaN x search terms) and assert the invariant for every view: the reviewer checked 231,784 views in seconds and also ran 1,000 random producer inputs against the producers' own evaluators. Derive every count from the rows and compare numbers with the producer's output, never with a second formula.

Before a K item adds files to an accepted namespace, find every consumer integrity check that runs git diff --exit-code against the accepted commit of that namespace: C021 integrity test 1 diffs the WHOLE C020 tree, so any committed addition fails it, and C021 test file is itself pinned (evidence.json:241). The correct move is the K rule: stop before adding anything, keep the drafted tests as a resume pack, and let the unblocking be its own card (U032: an append-only addendum for the consumer, never an edit of the sealed file).

Develop and verify a K item drafted tests OUTSIDE the repository (scratch copy of the accepted tests plus the real production file) when its namespace is blocked: the obstacle then costs no rework. w-K-C020 reached 100/100/100 with 148 tests and killed 44 of 44 mutants in scratch and left a resume pack under RUN/results/K-C020-resume.

A test that reads a file its child process rewrites with truncate-then-write races the reader: the C017 small-heap test failed about 15 percent of runs under load with the sampler wrote nothing. Write samples atomically (temp file plus rename), retry the read until it parses with a deadline, null-guard every dereference, and prove it with a 20-run, 5-parallel loop; a flake in a GREEN command is a defect because every consumer and the coverage gate inherit it.

Test a server-side stall with the attacker in a SEPARATE process: an in-process attacker and the server share one event loop, so the test passes while a real client is starved (C017: an endless chunked body from another process stalled the loop 2 to 5 s, the in-process test saw nothing). Measure the server event-loop lag (perf_hooks monitorEventLoopDelay inside the small-heap child) and the concurrent GET latency, and require the attacker sockets to be gone within a bound. Citing a lesson as applied needs the test that FAILS when the fix is removed.

A client page that validates only the one answer it sends (cancel) but prints every other server answer verbatim can be made to overstate: a tampered state view, reconcile answer or typed-failure reason showed everything cancelled and rolled back next to standing effects. Validate EVERY answer shape and RE-DERIVE the displayed wording from the facts (never print server prose), refuse an affirmative claim the facts do not support, and test every forged shape including malformed JSON and a malformed start answer (guard the render path with the same try/catch as the command).

child_process.spawn re-injects process.env.NODE_V8_COVERAGE into any child whose env object has no OWN NODE_V8_COVERAGE key, so deleting the key from a copy of process.env does not sanitize: the node --test runner then writes raw V8 coverage into the CALLER directory. Give the key an own, tool-owned value (or another mechanism that survives the re-injection) and prove it with a real-process test that runs the tool under an outer NODE_V8_COVERAGE=<dir> and asserts the directory stays empty; unit tests that assert the env OBJECT cannot see it.

A guard CLI must turn EVERY error into a typed failure and never leave an earlier pass behind: put a catch at the top of main (independent of NODE_OPTIONS=--unhandled-rejections, which makes an uncaught rejection exit 0), write a failure or started report first and on every error path so a reused --json path cannot keep a stale pass:true, and refuse to overwrite any existing file that is not a previous report of the tool (schema field), never a file the run enumerated or loaded.

Translating globs to a backtracking RegExp lets nested star patterns freeze enumeration (a 36-character name 9.9 s, each 4 characters multiply it by about 4): patterns come from manifests and callers, so use an iterative non-backtracking matcher, bound the enumeration work, and test with the reviewer patterns under a hard test timeout.

The refusal-close class (a refused request keeps the connection open and its body unread, so an endless chunked body of 1-byte chunks starves the event loop for seconds) was found in C044 (F2, F8), C017 (F2) and C009 (F1) AFTER the lesson existed: put the rule into structure, not memory. One refuse() function that every non-2xx path goes through (Connection: close, end, destroy the socket once flushed, stop reading), a table of every refusal status the server can emit with one test each, and a standard CROSS-PROCESS refusal-flood test (attacker in a separate process, server in a small-heap child, event-loop lag and concurrent GET latency under a bound): copy the C017 and C009 fix tests; U028 will extract the shared harness.

A retained-heap limit read at a fixed delay after a flood measures scheduling, not a leak: when the child is starved the in-flight request objects are still alive at the forced GC (C009 failed 1 in about 33 loaded runs). Poll until quiescent (server.getConnections idle, then a forced GC), use the minimum over a window or a margin over the measured baseline, and prove stability with an 8-parallel loop of at least 64 runs under heavy slots.

Node enforces server.headersTimeout and requestTimeout only every connectionsCheckingInterval (default 30 s): a configured 5 s timeout cuts a trickling client after about 30 s, and 256 such connections hold a capped listener for that long. Set connectionsCheckingInterval (for example 1000 ms) when you configure the timeouts, test the effective bound with a client that trickles one byte every 2 s, and state the real bound in the README.

A global state bound lets one identity starve another role (a conductor filled the 1000-entry bound and the operator approvals got 409 STATE_FULL) and an audit ring that records anonymous refusals loses every earlier denial after 250 anonymous requests: reserve headroom for privileged commands or quota per owner, and keep denials of identified subjects durable. Public reads (GET /v1/state) mean no per-owner read isolation: say so in the README so later cards (C010) do not assume it.

A guard whose removal passes every test is unproven: C042 deleting the maxConnections line or only the socket destroy after the flush still passed 82 of 82. For EVERY limit, cap and destroy rule, mutate the line away in a private copy and require a named test to fail; where the effect needs concurrency (the destroy mattered from about 27 attackers: 9 s stall versus 1.3 to 2.4 s)       run the attackers in a separate process.

Prove a persisted journal's tamper claim with an EXHAUSTIVE single-byte-flip test (every byte position x a few replacement values; the reviewer ran 7,284 flips in seconds): C042 accepted the final-newline flip and silently dropped the last record, and never reported a discarded tail. Report every discarded tail, and say in the README exactly what replay can and cannot detect (a re-chained forgery and boundary truncation are tamper-evident only       with an external anchor).

On Windows validate every user-supplied directory name: nul, con, prn, aux, com1 and lpt1 style device names and trailing dots or spaces are accepted by Node and create directories that plain Windows tools cannot delete. Reject them before creating anything.

TextDecoder strips a leading U+FEFF by default (ignoreBOM false), so decoding the bytes of a certificate subject or any identity string silently turns a BOM look-alike into an exact match: decode with ignoreBOM: true, compare exact code points, normalise nothing, and test the plain, hex-escaped and quoted forms plus every Unicode format character (Cf), joiner, zero-width character and variation selector at the start, middle and end.

A gate over a test run must require pass === tests > 0 with zero skipped, todo and cancelled, and positive evidence that the thing under test really ran (for a browser suite the version line the browser printed): a run that executes nothing must FAIL. node:test counts a file with no tests as 1 test and 1 pass, and an all-skipped or all-todo suite exits 0; the mutant that drops tests > 0 must be killed by a named test.

An output-path option must reject Windows reserved device names, trailing dots and spaces and any colon after the drive letter (an NTFS alternate data stream such as tracked.json:evil attaches to an EXISTING tracked file with exit 0), and must be checked BEFORE a long run starts: a failing check plus an existing target should cost seconds, not the minutes of the browser suites.

Silence from a system probe is not a clean result. An empty process table (or any empty answer from a helper that exited 0) must fail closed unless it contains something that must always be there (the caller's own pid), and a row whose key fact cannot be read (creation time null for 178 of 514 rows on a normal machine) must be reported as unverifiable, never silently dropped together with everything below it: a success-shaped empty answer is the failure mode of every kill, cleanup and verification tool.

A deadline has to be raced against every awaited adapter call by the CORE (a timer the core owns), not delegated to the adapter's cooperation: an adapter that ignores timeoutMs hangs the whole call although the README says everything is bounded. Test it with a never-settling adapter, and never pass a timer value above 2147483647 ms (Node clamps it to 1 ms).

Report an action as done only from evidence read AFTER the action (a confirming re-list), never from the actor's own return value: a lying kill adapter made 4 live processes `terminated`, and the mutant that skips the confirmation survived every hermetic test. Pin the confirmation with a named mutant.

A Windows parent process id is not authenticated: any same-user process can set it with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS. Ownership has to rest on identity recorded while the process was alive (pid plus creation time re-verified on the same handle before every kill); a late parent-link walk adopts a stranger whose ppid points into the tree, so state that direction in the README limits and never adopt the children of a refused entry.

On Windows {...process.env} is an ordinary object with case-SENSITIVE keys (SYSTEMROOT, WINDIR), while process.env itself is case-insensitive: code that looks up SystemRoot or windir by a literal name fails on a spread copy. Pass process.env itself or normalise names, and test both shapes.

Helper text embedded in a JavaScript string (a C# or PowerShell here-string) is invisible to Node coverage and to hermetic tests: mutate it too (7 mutants of the C# here-string, of which the real tests killed 3) using real, bounded, owned-fixture runs, and count its mutants in the evidence next to the line coverage.

A staleness rule that only looks at age passes a FUTURE date: the age is negative so neither the stale nor the stale-now check can fire. Parse dates strictly (one ISO form, real calendar dates, leap years, a time zone), bound them on BOTH sides with an injected clock, and test 2099, 2026-02-30, 2026-13-01, a locale spelling such as 12/20/2026 and the empty string.

An identifier or secret scanner must cover every SPELLING and every POSITION: a GUID as 32 hex digits, split by a newline, emphasis, zero-width or non-breaking characters; an e-mail as [at] or full-width @; and JSON object KEYS, not only values. Normalise first (NFKC, strip Cf format characters, fold non-breaking hyphens and spaces, strip markdown emphasis and escapes), list the forms you cover, and state the rest in the README limits: never claim any.

A deny-list of phrases proves nothing: a required resource row marked priced was accepted with free, no charge, n/a, included and an empty text. Validate rows with POSITIVE checks (a priced row needs a finite unit price above zero, a unit, a meter and a date; any other status must be an enumerated one) and test every zero-shaped spelling.

A guard only counts if it protects the SAME target it guards: parse commands with a quote-aware tokenizer and compare every delete target (resource group, subscription) with the guarded one; handle az.cmd and az.exe, && and | chains (each az command needs its own --subscription), an empty --subscription "", --subscription=value, line continuations and PowerShell cmdlets such as Remove-AzResourceGroup, and parse commands in every field and in the scripts, not only in the steps that name a guard.

A ceiling is a bound only if it is recomputed from the declared CAPS, not from the declared usage: raising a usage cap (egress 5000 GB = $435) left the $5 ceiling and the worst case unchanged and the packet was accepted. Compute the worst case from the caps and the unit prices inside the validator, require every declared usage at or below its cap, and make the raised cap fail unless the ceiling moves.

Bound every input of a checker: size, nesting depth and regex cost, and catch everything at the CLI. JSON nested 5000 deep threw an uncaught RangeError (a 15-line stack trace, no verdict) and a 200 KB token took 74 to 81 s in the e-mail and JWT patterns (quadratic); use iterative walkers or a depth cap, linear scanners, a size cap, and a one-line typed failure with a non-zero exit.

A date string built for a script the owner will run must use InvariantCulture: ToString with a custom format still turns the time separator into a dot in fi-FI and da-DK and changes the year in th-TH and ar-SA, so a parse of it throws or lands in the wrong year (the arming then fails, or arms the wrong time). Test the script under such cultures.

Pin the ABSENCE of output exactly: a fail-closed test that asserts only doesNotMatch(stdout, /allowed/) lets a handler that prints anything else pass. Assert stdout equals the empty string or an exact expected line (and the exit code and stderr), then mutate the handler to print extra text and require a named failure.

Find the consumers of an accepted namespace by every reference form before adding files to it: the capability/C0xx path, the module file names (require of probe.cjs), relative paths (..\C0xx), and the digest lists of other cards (dependency-pins.json, evidence-index addenda). A grep for the namespace path alone missed C018, which requires probe.cjs. Run every consumer, slow wrappers alone, and report honestly what could not be confirmed.

When an amendment relaxes an integrity rule from no change to additions allowed, enumerate the allowed additions by an ALLOW-LIST of path patterns instead of accepting any added path: an added package.json (type module), .gitattributes (EOL conversion), node_modules or a shadowing module changes behaviour without touching a pinned byte. Say which blind spots of the underlying git command remain.

Prove that a changed integrity rule detects everything the old rule detected by a DIFFERENTIAL matrix: run the same hostile scenarios (69 here: modify, delete, rename, move out, type change, mode change, intent-to-add, case variants, in the working tree, the index and a commit) through the old rule and the new one and show zero regressions and that only the intended additions flip, instead of arguing it from the diff.

Never assert an absolute wall-clock event-loop lag or latency bound in a test that shares a loaded machine: the OS scheduler dominates (a bare 400-and-close server showed 490 ms, 11 s and 37 s at 10, 60 and 200 attacker sockets while other agents ran at 100% CPU, so a 9.5 s bound failed 4 of 6 runs and a 150 ms per socket bound would pass a regression). Assert STRUCTURE (every refused socket is closed by the server within a bound of its answer, connections reach 0, the bytes parsed after a refusal are bounded, the service answers a GET after the flood), the server child CPU time per attacker socket, and compare against a naive control run in the same test under the same load (a ratio, never seconds); the test must fail on the naive keep-alive server and pass 20 loops under load.

An accessibility checker must be attacked with fixtures of every class it claims to catch, not only with the defects it was written against: a mouse-only div role=button without tabindex, button or link with tabindex=-1 outside a composite widget, a focusable button inside an aria-hidden ancestor (look at ancestors, not the element), role=status with aria-live=off or aria-hidden, a role that does not match the element, a standalone checkbox or radio without aria-checked all gave ZERO findings. Derive reachability independently of the focusable set it validates (a tab walk built from the same set can never find an unreachable control).

Mutate every guard line with a SYSTEMATIC generator (every statement and every single condition), not a chosen list: 43 chosen mutants hid 16 page and 11 checker survivors that a generated run of 81 and 34 mutants found (data-about never set made the checker announcement rules vacuous; result facts never shown because the tests read textContent of HIDDEN elements: assert visibility, not text). List every equivalent mutant with its reason and report killed and survived counts.

A page must BIND an answer to its request and bound its wait: a perfectly valid envelope of ANOTHER step (other key, other lease, 9 units) answering an Inspect was shown, announced as success and its key adopted into the page state, and a request that is accepted but never answered left the page aria-busy forever with the recovery controls removed. Check the identity fields of every answer against the request, range-check numerics against derivable facts, and give every pending request a deadline, an abort, a typed no-answer failure, an announcement and a recovery control.

PowerShell variable names are case-INSENSITIVE and loop variables leak into the enclosing scope: a loop variable $run overwrote $RUN and broke a heavy-slot release in finally (K-C020), and a counter $c reused in a harness crashed it at its after controls and lost the whole report (U033). Use distinct, prefixed names ($RUNDIR, $ctl) in every harness, slot script and long runner, and keep the first failing report on disk before any later step can crash.

Swap a reviewed publisher in atomically and keep rollback: copy the reviewed file next to the live one, verify its SHA-256 against the reviewed hash, replace with File.Replace (which also writes a backup), verify the live hash, then re-pin line 1 of every GO file (keep the old ones of void SHAs out of the way) and verify them all against the live hash in one sweep; workers verify line 1 before publishing and poll on a mismatch.

A request PIPELINED BEHIND A REFUSAL still runs its effects: Node parses every pipelined request of one TCP read and emits each request event before the first response has finished, response.socket is null for a queued response (endConnection(null) is a no-op) and destroying the socket on the refusal finish event is too late (a refused GET plus a valid POST in one write applied the whole preset and a resize behind 7 refusal kinds; two writes 5 ms apart do not). Mark the connection SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the one central refuse() using request.socket, drop every later request at the top of the handler, serialize per connection when a refusal can be decided after an await, and test with raw sockets in ONE write (see orders/_PIPELINING.md); a close-after-refusal test that only checks the Connection header and the closing socket cannot see it.

An evidence-integrity test must iterate EVERY manifest of EVERY capture: a filter that skipped every JSON under raw left four of five captures (38 pinned inputs each: README, production files, tests) unchecked while the README said it recomputed every hash, so one README byte and one production byte changed undetected. Write a tamper test per capture kind (a README byte, a production byte, a test byte, a stream byte, a pin) in a scratch copy that must fail by name, and state that a consistent rewrite of manifest plus inputs is not detectable.

A layer on top of a persisted service must verify EVERY acknowledged step against the system of record at load and on every inspect, resume and re-run, not only the pending one: after a flipped final newline or a cut step journal the preset answered COMPLETED with three standing effects while the step service held ten units, under a README sentence that said it cannot happen. Answer a typed unconfirmed or interrupted result with the honest listing, expose the discarded tail, and never document a cross-check the code does not perform.

On Windows a test that expects the typed answer to a header flood races an RST: Node default clientError path writes the 431 and destroys the socket while unread data is still arriving, and the reset can discard the 431 before the client reads it (6 failures in 96 runs at 8-way, also in the first publication). Either install a clientError handler that stops reading first, writes the answer and ends the socket after the flush, or assert an empty answer plus a CLOSED connection; then prove it with an 8-way loop of at least 64 runs on a busy machine, because a worker loop of 8 on a quiet machine cannot see a 1 in 16 race.

Give a sealed tool an APPEND-ONLY extension path for its allow-list before other cards adopt it: if the only documented way to extend the qualified set edits a pinned file, the tool own evidence test goes red (19 of 23 manifests pinned the data file, 11 the README, 21 a production file, and the verifier pinned itself) and no content of the file keeps the namespace green after the next browser update. Seal the data file, read hash-chained addendum lines after it, make the verifier amendment-aware (pin the sealed file and the helper by raw SHA-256 INSIDE the test), and execute every README procedure in a scratch copy before writing that it breaks no test.

A tool evidence test must verify only what lives INSIDE its own namespace: manifests whose inputs are files of ANOTHER card (20 capability/C031 files each) made the suite red whenever that card changed legitimately and in every scratch copy that lacks it (the reviewer own copy failed 1 of 151). Verify external inputs by their recorded identity (commit and digests consistent with the archived transcript), re-verify them only in an explicitly named strict mode against git cat-file blob of the accepted commit, never against the working tree, and keep the default suite green in a copy of the namespace without the other card and without .git.

Run a RED or any experiment against an UNFIXED tool with the working directory in a scratch folder, never in the repository root: the old --json followed the Windows device name NUL into a real file and left NUL and nul.json untracked in the root (ordinary tools cannot delete a file named NUL: use the long-path prefix) where any git add -A would sweep them in. Check git status for strays after every RED run.

A central send() is not central while Node answers requests ITSELF: an unknown Expect header gets Node own 417 (the handler never runs, maxRequestsPerSocket only adds a Connection: close header, the socket stays open and the dumped body keeps being parsed), a request without Host gets a Node 400 and parse errors go to clientError. Install checkExpectation, checkContinue and clientError listeners that route every one of these into the one refusal path (typed answer, close, stop reading), add a ROW for each Node-own answer to the refusal table with a naive-server RED, and mutate the missing listener.

Do not rely on server.maxRequestsPerSocket to stop a request pipelined behind a refusal: it is not applied to HTTP/1.0 requests and its counter is not advanced by Node own no-Host 400, so one write [refusal HTTP/1.1][valid mutation HTTP/1.0] applied the mutation behind 27 of 29 refusal kinds (141 of 400 cases). Keep your own per-socket guard at the top of the handler regardless of the HTTP version and test every pair in BOTH framings (1.1 and 1.0) in a separate server process, with the journal hash and revision unchanged.

A view check that cross-checks only the lines that carry the CURRENT key accepts forged lines that omit it: viewCheck compared cancel-decided and reconciled lines with the current actionId only, so a journal pane line rewritten without an actionId (cancel-decided COMPENSATED, compensation-effect, action-completed) or a null-action view with a deciding line was shown next to contradicting facts, in the DOM stub and in real Edge. Re-derive EVERY displayed line of EVERY type from the facts (a line without the key is refused where the type requires one) and differential-test the derivation against the real engine.

The WebSocket upgrade event bypasses the HTTP request handler: Node emits upgrade for an upgrade request pipelined behind a refused request on the same socket, so a closing mark checked only in the request handler lets a valid Upgrade plus a masked hello frame create a hub session behind ANY refusal (10 of 15 variants on C026). Check the mark in the upgrade listener as well, destroy the socket there, and test with a raw write [refused request][valid Upgrade][masked hello frame] asserting the session count unchanged.

Scope a defect class across accepted cards with ONE parametrised probe run read-only from a scratch snapshot (git archive HEAD of the namespaces), one server at a time, with positive controls (RED on the HEAD snapshot, GREEN on a scratch-patched copy and on work-in-progress copies) before writing any fix item: three of six servers were being edited while the audit ran, and a K item cannot carry such tests because they fail until server.cjs changes (so each vulnerable accepted card needs a fix item with the RED archived against the HEAD bytes).

Pins of files of ANOTHER namespace recorded as raw working-tree bytes fail in every fresh checkout: five accepted files with the attribute text eol=lf were pinned with the CRLF bytes of the Windows owner tree, so 2 of 70 tests failed in a clone (converting just those five files to CRLF gave 70 of 70). Record the raw and the LF-normalized SHA-256 and the git blob, accept either form (or compare the LF-normalized one) for files outside the owned namespace, and prove the suite in a scratch tree built from git archive (LF bytes) and in its CRLF conversion before publishing.

A pure model must never return a shared mutable object: answer.flags (one object per position), the marks array and, for an unfrozen saved run, entries, entry and source were aliased, so a consumer write changed every later answer and note (a GAP BEFORE note vanished) while verify stayed green because it compared only state, mark and tallies. Freeze or copy every returned object in the assembler, make verify compare every field the model returns, and test with a GENERIC aliasing walker (mutate every reachable object of every public return value in strict mode, frozen and unfrozen inputs, then compare all later outputs) instead of chosen examples.

A display oracle must compare EVERY rendered line: assertShown compared 8 of 16 state lines, so four reviewer mutants (Reconnects, Resyncs, Connection, Epoch changes) survived seven suites while the README claimed every DOM action is checked against an independent fold. Enumerate the rendered ids from the DOM and assert that the set equals the set the oracle compares (a new line fails until it is compared), and generate mutants systematically over the render code (extends L-0172).

A builder that promises a typed refusal and never a throw needs a seeded fuzz over hostile JS values (sparse arrays and holes, undefined, throwing getters, cycles, prototype keys), and its producer metadata must be cross-checked against the recorded events: new Array(3) threw a TypeError, a hole built 3 positions and then threw at stateAt, and a producer last sequence of 5 on a recording of 22 events built COMPLETE and said 22 events of 5 produced.

A test must assert the property its name and README claim: startLocal binds only 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port asserted only port greater than 0, so a hard-coded listen(48151) survived 148 tests. For every claim about binding (loopback only, ephemeral port) start two instances at once or read the bound address twice and assert the exact property, then mutate the listen call and require a named failure.

Never build a user-folder path by hand: Join-Path with USERPROFILE and Desktop does not exist when the Desktop is redirected (a known-folder move), so Set-Content threw, the catch only added a sentence to the dialog and the promised persistent alarm file was never written. Resolve it with [Environment]::GetFolderPath(Desktop), fall back to the temp folder, say in the text where the file is, and make the scenario test assert that the file EXISTS after a failure with a normal, a redirected and a missing folder.

A pasted multi-line block must stay safe when the host runs it statement by statement: never end it with an irreversible disarm (Unregister-ScheduledTask of the only automatic backstop) that does not depend on the verification, because pasted as one unit PowerShell stops at the first failing guard but a host that continues after a failed statement removes the backstop. Put the disarm after the verification section and guard it explicitly (az group exists must answer false, else throw and keep the backstop armed), and make the validator require that guard for any Unregister, Disable or Stop of the teardown task.

A checker must read an option the way the tool reads it: az (argparse) keeps the LAST occurrence of a repeated option while the validator read the FIRST, so a guarded first --name followed by --name other-rg passed and the delete acted on the other group. Reject any repeated option in a guarded command and allow only a CLOSED list of statement shapes in a guarded step, so redefined guard functions, reassigned variables and indirection (Process Start, ScriptBlock Create, Invoke-Expression, dot-sourcing) are refused by construction instead of by an open-ended deny list.

A size and depth cap does not bound the work: a parser that copies the whole block stack into every statement retains about 3 n squared bytes (38,000 nested openers in a 115 KB script killed the CLI with heap out of memory, exit 134), and NFKC normalisation of a long run of combining marks of different classes is super-quadratic (160,000 marks took 185 s; 1.9 MB of JSON took 371 s) while the validator folded every string about seven times. Keep a parent pointer per block, cap nesting and combining-mark runs, fold each string once and share the result, set a total character budget, and prove it structurally (a child process with a capped heap, counters of normalize calls and folded characters), never with an absolute time bound; do not write the word linear in a README without measuring the adversarial shapes.

When a checker over an open language (PowerShell, markdown) is rejected a second time for NEW bypass classes, stop adding deny rules: the third review found duplicate options, redefined guards, indirection, a parser memory blow-up and a normalisation DoS in code that already had 559 tests. Switch to positive designs (a closed list of statement shapes with closed parameter vocabularies, an exact or whole-section comparison against the reviewed text, typed caps before any expensive work), narrow the README claims to the listed shapes (never catches everything), and say that the checker is a tripwire for accidental edits, not a proof.

Ownership of a process must be POSITIVE and fixed at launch: an owned tree that adopts every new direct child of the caller for the whole session ends another live session browser (two sessions in one process: A.terminate or A.close killed B, 0 of 8 processes alive and its page closed; a second terminate on a closed session ended the NEXT session; an unrelated child was ended). Adopt new roots only inside the serialised startup window, then refresh descendants of the recorded identities only, and test two live sessions closed in FIFO and LIFO order, a repeated terminate and an unrelated child, hermetically and once in a real browser. Any tool that kills by recent children is a concurrency bug when agents share a machine.

An abort signal must be honoured at every await: the startup checked signal.aborted once, awaited a slow baseline read (2 s, tens of seconds under load), started the work and only then attached the abort listener, so an abort during the baseline or while queued behind the lock was lost and close() waited 74 to 109 s for the whole open. Attach the listener before the first await, re-check aborted after every await, and test with controllable baseline and lock adapters on a virtual clock.

A real-browser test must not assert that EVERY recorded process is still alive: short-lived Chromium utility processes exit on their own (the worker own hint said so), the assertion failed in a review run and, because the test had no finally, the failure leaked a live Edge tree and a scratch directory. Assert the root and a lower bound, wrap every real session in try and finally that ends the OWN session, and add a test that injects a failing assertion and proves the cleanup ran. Default budgets must also be derived from the remaining overall budget or their sum stated: three sequential defaults (60 s, 60 s, 30 s) put the rejection at deadline + 120 s.

A tool that writes its report to a path the caller names must survive two concurrent runs: the loser failure handler replaced the winner file, so two passing runs ended as two exit 1 and a failure report at the shared path (fail-closed but spurious). On a changed-identity conflict do not replace the file (the other writer keeps its report), say in the README that every run needs its own path, and test two concurrent runs with one path.

A structural cost counter that is computed from the loop bounds is a model, not a measurement: a constant-factor or quadratic slowdown that the counter does not mirror survives every structural test (two reviewer mutants did). Count real iterations inside the loops, or compare CPU time with a naive control on one large input in the same run, and keep a mutant that adds hidden work to the list of required kills.

Never read another namespace data file directly when that namespace has an append-only addendum: three lifecycle test files read the sealed qualified.json and asserted the installed Edge major was in it, so they would fail the moment an addendum added Edge 157 although the owning API (readQualified, qualifyEdge) says qualified. Call the owning API, and add a test that fails when a file outside the owner names the sealed data file outside a comment.

A test file must fit the per-file timeout with a 4x slowdown, not only be assertion-structural: a process-spawning file that takes 15 s quiet took 33 s at 4 CPU burners and 56 s at 8 and was cancelled by the 60 s file cap inside the whole suite, and 8 parallel copies timed out 32 of 32. Share one server child and one naive control per file instead of a pair per subtest, cut subtests to the classes that matter (one per code path), split a matrix file by framing into files of about 12 s quiet, remove waits longer than the file cap, and loop UNDER 8 burners you started yourself (record their PIDs), not only on a machine that is merely busy.

A README importer contract that three later cards will rely on must be TESTED against the module: it documented admit.refuse(socket, code, { immediate }) although the function takes two arguments and immediate occurs nowhere, so a consumer passing the option silently got the queue-respecting behaviour. Add a test that checks every function and option named in the importer section against the real exports (a documented name that is not exported fails) and derive every figure in the README from the evidence.

A Node-own answer decided at PARSE time (checkExpectation answering 417 for Expect nonsense) runs outside a per-socket lane: with TWO or more legitimate requests pipelined BEFORE it the refusal clears the queue, the earlier request is dropped, Node cannot flush the 417 and the connection stays OPEN ([G][X] is fine, [G][G][X] gets only 200 and never closes; 128 sockets of about 150 bytes pin a 128-connection cap). Route every Node-own answer (417, no-Host 400, clientError, checkContinue) through the SAME lane or drop only the entries AFTER the refusing request so the earlier ones are answered in order, then the typed refusal, then close and destroy; put two and three legitimate requests BEFORE every Node-own refusal in the matrix, in a separate server process, in both framings, plus a structural 128-socket resource test.

A binding check must not skip a field because the forged value is null: a valid envelope of another step (other lease, 9 units) with idempotencyKey, validatedInput and inputSha256 set to null was accepted and announced as Succeeded because bindingProblem skipped its key and input checks when the key was null (the pinned validator allows a null key on a success envelope). Refuse a succeeded or accepted envelope with a null key when the request carried a key, and test every null and missing combination of every bound field.

Decide a mutant that makes a loop endless by an ITERATION BOUND, not by a wall-clock timeout: on a saturated machine a timeout cannot tell an infinite loop from starvation (the harness had to call it undecided), but with a loop counter or a bounded fake clock injected into the mutated code all 7 timed-out mutants died by named tests and the two bound-only controls passed. Report such mutants as killed-by-bound with the bound named, and keep plain timeouts as undecided.

Dropping a pipelined request is not a refusal unless something is WRITTEN or the socket is STOPPED: a handler that returns at once for every request after the first on a socket (taken.has(socket)) answers nothing and never pauses or destroys it, so while the first request is pending the parser keeps queueing IncomingMessage and ServerResponse objects with no backpressure (about 1.8 KB each): 23.6k requests (1 MB) hung a 48 MB-heap child and 45.9k aborted it with out-of-memory, whereas a queued 503 per later request made Node pause the socket and the first fix stayed responsive. At the first dropped request pause the socket, count the dropped requests and destroy it after the first answer is flushed or after a small constant, and test with a capped heap: a pending first request plus 50k pipelined requests keeps the child alive, its heap bounded and a legitimate GET answered.

A fix that removes a defect class can introduce the opposite one: the second C017 fix closed every request-runs-behind-a-refusal path and thereby created a resource-exhaustion path in the same function. After each pipelining fix probe the OPPOSITE failure in a capped-heap separate process (what does the server do with the requests it dropped, how much memory does a pending first request plus tens of thousands of later ones cost, is a legitimate GET still answered afterwards) and keep the first fix as the A/B control when the attack is new.

A validator README limits list is part of its contract and reviewers audit it as such: after four rounds the U001 validator was accepted, but the reviewer still found five accepted-by-design families the list did not name (uncompared title and intro prose, a 4 to 9 times NFKC cost multiplier inside the caps, duplicate and unknown top-level JSON keys, a BOM giving exit 2, prose deletes). Probe your own validator for what an OK does NOT mean, write each family into the limits list and pin each sentence by a test that fails when the behavior changes.

lessons.evidence: reviews/U001.fix3.verdict.json (Q6); git grep at HEAD: 911 text files carry the local Windows user name
lessons.text: The repository is PUBLIC and the recorders write absolute local paths into manifests and transcripts, so the local Windows user name (and the session id) end up in committed evidence (24 of 330 files of testing/quality; 911 text files of the repository at HEAD, mostly learning/ and capability/). Sealed evidence cannot be scrubbed without breaking its hash pins, so only NEW files can be fixed: use repository-relative paths or placeholders in the command lines and README text you record, and scan your added files for the user name and session id before publishing (rule 15 of the worker rules; line 16 of the pre-publication checklist).

Node parses a WHOLE 64 KB read (about 1,600 tiny pipelined requests) before any lane can cut the socket, so every socket whose first request is still held keeps about 6 MB of request and response objects until that request ends: a child with a 48 MB heap survives 3 and 5 such sockets and dies at 8 (exit 134, C059 probe). The growth is PER SOCKET and capped by the connection cap, not per request after the first read. Do not claim memory is bounded outright: probe 3 sockets (the F24 shape), say in the README limits what one pending socket costs and what the connection cap bounds, and treat growth with the NUMBER OF REQUESTS after the first read as the real defect.
lessons.evidence: results/C059.json (F24 probe, C059-probe-f24); results/C022.json and results/C010.json (3-socket probes pass)

lessons.text: Publishing partial work at the budget end is fine only if every committed test passes: C059 published with two integrity rules RED by design (they pin a full mutation campaign and a load loop that were never captured on the final bytes), which makes every GREEN claim false and guarantees a rejection. Leave the pinning test out and list the missing capture in notChecked and the README limits, or make the test report an explicit uncaptured status that cannot be mistaken for a pass (rule 16); capture the evidence in the NEXT amendment, never pin evidence you do not have.
lessons.evidence: orders/_CONTROLLER-UPDATE.md rule 16; results/C059.json (integrity-fix rules red on the published tree)

lessons.text: Make test cost a property of the structure, never of the load: three rejections of C009 (F9c) came from process-spawning test files that cost 16 to 24 s alone and therefore hit the 60 s per-file cap whenever the shared machine was busy; the accepted fix shares one server child and one persistent attacker per file, runs 8 cells per row where about 600 were run, splits the 605-cell matrix into three files by framing and uses count-only checks, so each file costs 2.6 to 5.2 s alone and the whole suite 423/423 in 79 s. Only a measurable criterion ends a rejection loop: a plain whole-suite run on the machine as it is under the file cap, plus a loop under burners recorded as a finding with figures; a criterion that depends on other agents load cannot be met by any worker.

A README that cites an evidence file or a figure must be checked against the repository: the accepted C009 README cited a per-file duration_ms in a TAP file and a suite-under-load.json that never existed, and read as if the load loops passed while every loop of the final bytes failed by the cap and only 2 of 7 were named. Add a test that every evidence path a README names exists and is pinned, and write one README sentence per failed loop family: the honest statement belongs in the README, not only in a NOTE file and the result file.

A refusal that waits for a lane entry must prove that entry can finish: U039 made refuseUnparsed answer a Node-decided error only after lanes.get(socket) settled, but when Node reports the error for the request that is STILL READING ITS BODY (a bad chunk size, a Content-Length body cut by the request timeout, a client FIN in mid-body) that entry is the request own, parked in readBody for a body that cannot end, so the typed refusal waited for itself: nothing written, the socket open until the 90 s idle timeout, 128 sockets of 114 bytes pinning the connection cap (the accepted parent answered 400 in 18 to 48 ms). The sound rule is the one C009 http-io.cjs already has: the request Node was still receiving (request.complete false) is the one that failed, a queued one never runs and a running one is answered at once, everything else waits only for the requests BEFORE it. For every await in a refusal path ask what finishes it and whether it can be the refused request itself; put incomplete-message kinds (bad chunk size, short body then silence, short body then FIN, behind 0 to 2 complete requests, after Expect: 100-continue) into the matrix in a separate process with a server-side connection count that must return to zero. C043 has the lighter variant (no typed answer, closed at the request timeout of about 5 s): follow-up U048.
lessons.evidence: reviews/U039.verdict.json (F1); results/U039-review/rep.cjs; scratch probe of C043 by the controller

lessons.text: A fix that was built BEFORE a lesson existed must be re-checked against that lesson before it is published, even by a publish-only worker: U040 was finished and verified before L-0209 (a dropped pipelined request must be answered or the socket stopped) was written, and a publish-only order then published the unchanged bytes hours after the broadcast; the reviewer found the very flood crash the lesson describes (a 48 MB child dies at 3 sockets, exit 134). When a lesson is recorded, list every unpublished work item it applies to and add the check to ITS order (here: run the F24 probe before publishing), and treat a publish-only order as a new chance to ask what the newest lessons say about the tree.

Validate-then-use on a caller-supplied object is a time-of-check to time-of-use hole: U006 validated the options, spread them into the startup and read them again in wrapSession, so a getter that answers 1000 twice and oops the third time made the third read throw AFTER the browser tree was already live, and close() reported clean:true while 5 of 5 processes were alive, behind a README sentence that said every option is read exactly ONCE. Take ONE frozen snapshot of the options at the public boundary, pass the snapshot everywhere, end whatever the startup produced when a later step throws, and test with a lying getter and a Proxy; a sentence that says read once is a claim that needs that test.

A test that returns early is a VACUOUS PASS, not a skip: C017 guarded its END-state test with if (!ended()) return;, so with no evidence/pins.json the runner printed a plain ok (1 ms, # skipped 0), the 391 of 391 figure and the README counted a test that asserted nothing, and the test would have FAILED had it run (one assertion group of 28: an undecided mutant). The README prose was honest; the test output and the result figure were not. Use test(name, { skip: reason }) so TAP prints # SKIP and # skipped N and state the figure as N passed plus M skipped; better, make the condition reachable and prove by a meta-test (run the file in a scratch copy without the precondition and assert the output says SKIP) that it can never pass silently.

Pin each capture to the files it EXECUTES (subject, helpers, its own tooling), never to the whole namespace: C017 pins the same 94 namespace files in every manifest (green, seven coverage runs, twelve loops, two generator runs, two browser runs), so a one-line fix of an unrelated verifier forces recapturing the twelve loops and the 40-minute generator run, and every review round costs about 3 hours of recapture. Keep verifiers, the README and descriptive fields out of the pinned input set (pin them last in one pins.json), or supersede a verifier edit through an append-only addendum, so that a documentation or verifier fix needs only the captures whose subject changed.

A validator must refuse every value its protection layer cannot protect: C014 accepted a 5-character contact name (the regex admitted 5 to 61) while the redactor registers values by exact match only from 6 characters, so the accepted name reached anonymous public trace, runs and bundle although 601 socket probes and 87,000 planted contexts found no WHOLE canary of the worker's high-entropy design. Make the invariant explicit and testable: whatever the validator ACCEPTS is registered by value (or is a shape) and appears in no public byte after a normal flow, proved by a boundary sweep of every protected field at min-1, min, min+1 and max, and refuse (typed error) rather than lower a threshold that would mask ordinary text.

In a masker the order of operations decides what survives: replacing registered sub-parts (name parts, the e-mail local part) BEFORE the whole-value check consumes the part the whole-value view needed, so a URL-encoded e-mail left its domain and a URL-encoded name left its given name, behind a README sentence that said the WHOLE value is masked (fail closed); run the whole-value check on the ORIGINAL text first, then the exact replacements. Regex shape guards need a test per QUANTIFIER and class that asserts no character of a long e-mail local part or of a 32, 33 and 39 digit hex run survives, plus a generator of regex-literal mutants, because mutating {1,64} to {1,2} or {32,} to {320,} survived 116 tests that only asserted the whole sample was gone, behind a README sentence that said every literal limit is pinned by a named test. A sweep with canaries whose parts are all long enough cannot see fragment classes: include short-part names and e-mails.

Isolation tests need a subject that EXISTS in two scopes: C022 had a correct tenant model and correct code, but its tests, and even its seeded property run, only ever created users that belong to ONE tenant, so replacing the iterable live(tenant) by sessions.values() in revokeUser (a revoke in tenant alder ending the same user's session in tenant birch) survived 25 test files, and the generator could not even produce that mutant because it does not mutate iteration sources or call arguments. For every operation that selects sessions, users or resources by a name, build a fixture where the SAME name is active in two tenants, test both directions, start every property seed with such a subject, and add a mutation class for iterables and call arguments (the unscoped sibling of every scoped accessor).

Equivalent needs a RUNNABLE demonstration and UNDECIDED is a survivor: C059 excused the mutant that deletes decide(socket) in refuseMalformed as equivalent after three mutation runs that ended without a named failing test (the load made server.test.cjs hit its per-test cap), on the mechanism that a handler queued behind a refused and destroyed socket fails its loopback check. The mechanism is false: Node caches remoteAddress once a request was read, so the queued handler still passed and a body-less cancel queued behind a parse error cancelled a step in flight on ANOTHER connection (the real service answers 201 and the step succeeds, the mutant answers 409 and the step ends cancelled), while 294 of 294 tests passed on the mutant. Never accept an equivalence from reasoning about the platform: probe the observable on the real and on the mutated tree, classify a run without a named assertion failure (a timeout, a crash, a file-level failure) as UNDECIDED and rerun it with the documented cap on a quiet machine, and write equivalent as written (reasoning only) in the README unless a test passes on both trees and demonstrates the platform fact.

Test the FAMILY and assert the effect on SHARED state: the pipelining suites queued invalid or body-carrying requests behind a refusal and asserted the answers of the refused connection, so no test queued a body-less state change (POST /v1/steps/key/cancel) behind a refusal while a step was in flight on another connection, and the deletion of the single call that drops what waits behind a Node parse error survived 294 tests. For every guard that must stop the later requests of a connection, write a table over (refusal kind x queued mutation x write shape: the same write, a later write) and assert what ANOTHER connection can observe (the in-flight step still succeeds, ledger and journal unchanged), with a gate the test releases instead of a timed hold, so that the assertion is an absence proved after a barrier and never a duration.

Test the DEFAULT limits, not only the small limits the tests configure: C010 copied the C009 defaults (idleMs = headerMs = 5000), so the socket idle timeout wins the race against the header timeout and a stalled header or body is closed SILENTLY at the default limits (no typed 408, no audit record; a coin flip between 408 and silence in a child process), although the feature file and the README matrix list 408; every test configured headerMs 300 and checkMs 50 and never saw it. Order timeouts so that the typed answer can win (the idle timeout above the header timeout plus the check interval), assert that order on the limits read back from the server, and add one default-limits test for a stalled header and one for a stalled body.

When a worker declares an explicit UNCAPTURED mutation gap on the minute-210 rule, let the reviewer run the unexecuted remainder inside a mutation slot and judge the survivors by guard class: C010 left 84 of 806 mutants unexecuted, the reviewer ran them in about an hour with 4 workers (resume, then --retest with the guard test files, then --finalize: 779 killed, 17 equivalent, 10 survived, none an ownership guard) and accepted with ONE follow-up item that closes the campaign, instead of rejecting for a gap whose closure by the next worker would cost another recapture of every pinned manifest (3 to 4 hours). A survivor in an ownership, tenant, session, redaction or budget guard is still a major.

COUNT the assertions per test with a preload instead of reading for early returns: C022 generated one refusal-close test per row of a status table and guarded one row with `if (entry.only11 && entry.nodeOwn && entry.code === 'METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED') return;`, so the CONNECT row executed zero assertions, passed on every server and even passed in the archived RED against the naive stub (ok 387 while 382 others failed), and it survived two review rounds of reading; the reviewer's assertion-counting preload over the whole suite (wrap node:assert and node:assert/strict and the test context assert, report every test that ran with n = 0) found it in one pass. Before publishing, run such a preload over every suite, list every n = 0 test and make each one assert or register it with { skip: reason } so that the plain run prints # SKIP; in a generated table a row that cannot be tested must be a named skip, never a return.

An UNEXPLAINED failure of a loop is a defect until a reproduction loop says otherwise, and a count of what a CLIENT managed to read after the server closed is a race on Windows: C014 published with one process-flood failure in 120 loop runs described as unexplained, and the reviewer reproduced it at once (4 failures in 120 runs, 3 concurrent, no burners, the same 3 percent) because the test asserted that the client read at least 6 typed 403 answers while the reset that follows the server close discards unread answers; in every failing run the server had ended 12 of 12 sockets and every status was 403 or 0. Assert on the SERVER side (a counter incremented where the refusal is written, equal to the number of attackers after quiescence) or on one non-flooding probe socket per shape that nothing resets, never on a client-side count of surviving answers; and before publishing, loop any file that failed once at least 72 times at 3 concurrent with the assertion message printing the observed state, and do not publish with the failure still unexplained.

A masker needs the UNION of all matches and ONE source of truth for the encodings it claims: replacing secret by secret with split and join leaves a fragment when occurrences OVERLAP (secrets abcdefgh and efghijkl over abcdefghijkl give [redacted]ijkl); compute the union of the intervals of every verbatim occurrence (indexOf advancing by one character) and replace each merged interval once, and check a model of it in a randomized test over small alphabets that force overlaps.
