hints.text: The earlier marked-tree recovery probe failed while a watchdog-only probe passed. Use a marked Node child tree, not Edge. Do not edit isolated.cjs: every test pins its SHA.

libuv puts non-detached Node children in a kill-on-close job of their parent: ending the parent ends them at once and a racing TerminateProcess fails access denied (adapter maps it to gone). Fixtures use detached:true for orphans.

Every hidden-console Node process (windowsHide, not detached) has a conhost.exe child. It is a descendant and owned: expect it in snapshots as terminated or alreadyGone and assert sets against an independent table, never process counts.

Windows identity: Toolhelp snapshot plus GetProcessTimes (100 ns FILETIME) in one PowerShell 5.1 Add-Type helper; verify and terminate on one handle. CIM took 1 to 4 s and truncates to 1 us: never compare it with .NET StartTime.

Edge root without a name: list direct children of process.pid before chromium.launch, diff after, snapshotTree(pid, adapters, {ownerPid: process.pid}), refreshTree at checkpoints, terminateOwned only after close times out (>= 30 s).

OpenProcess(TERMINATE) can be denied for sandboxed or elevated browser children: the adapter reports error:open:5 and the process stays a survivor. U005 and U006 must fail the close on survivors or errors, never retry by name or marker.

Real-process oracle without pids: fixtures hold loopback connections the OS closes when they die (ping/pong for alive) plus an independent read-only process table; fixtures exit on socket EOF, so a crashed test leaves nothing.

A naive kill RED is safe by construction when its only destructive path is adapters.kill behind a guard that throws for any pid the test did not create and the naive kill refuses to run without that guard (kill-by-marker and by-name REDs).

tree.cjs 100/95.81/100 and windows.cjs 100/94.74/95.83 from hermetic tests alone (virtual-clock FakeOS, fake spawn, 150-seed chaos); real tests add no coverage need. Node cannot measure the embedded PowerShell and C# text.

Twenty sequential real runs took 776 s (23 to 99 s each at 100% CPU) and slots can all be busy for minutes: take the heavy slot once for the loop; the lock goes stale after 40 minutes, so keep a slot window under 35.

U007 and U008: add new files only under testing\browser\lifecycle, inject adapters, reuse tests/support/fake-os.cjs, fake-spawn.cjs and scenario.cjs (startScenario, guardAdapters); never edit isolated.cjs.

When GREEN exposes a flaw in a test fixture, the first RED stays archived unchanged; re-archive the RED on the final tests under new names (red-04 to red-06) against the same naive module and explain both sets in the README.

U005 and U006 consume tree.cjs and windows.cjs READ-ONLY (never edit them: U004 tests and evidence pin their bytes): createWindowsAdapters({ env: process.env }), snapshotTree(rootPid, adapters, { ownerPid }) while the tree is alive, refreshTree at checkpoints, terminateOwned(snapshot, { timeoutMs, adapters }) returning { terminated, alreadyGone, survivors, refused, errors }. Fix-before-reliance findings F1 (an EMPTY process table is accepted: every entry comes back alreadyGone with no error), F2 (a descendant with an unreadable creation time is silently dropped with everything below it) and F5 (system pids and foreign roots are not refused, ownerPid is optional, the adapter forwards the caller's pid) are to be enforced at the composition level by a new file of the lifecycle bundle, test-first, with a named mutant per rule, until a later item folds them into tree.cjs.

createWindowsAdapters({ env }) looks SystemRoot and windir up case-sensitively: on Windows a plain copy {...process.env} is an ordinary object whose keys are SYSTEMROOT and WINDIR, so it throws ERR_PLATFORM (fails closed). Pass process.env itself (its lookups are case-insensitive) or add the names explicitly, and test both.

A finite timeoutMs above 2147483647 ms makes Node clamp the helper timer to 1 ms (TimeoutOverflowWarning) so list and kill fail at once with ERR_TIMEOUT: cap or reject such values. terminateOwned and snapshotTree await the adapters without racing the deadline: an adapter that ignores timeoutMs hangs the call (the shipped windows.cjs ends its helper with its own timer, so the shipped composition is bounded: timeoutMs 1 returned in 20 ms and 300 in 333 ms).

`terminated` is attested by the KILL ADAPTER, not by the process table: a lying adapter made 4 live processes terminated with only ERR_DEADLINE in errors, and mutant M24 (a kill marked confirmed without the confirming re-list) survives all 34 hermetic tests. Five more hermetic mutants live: M16 (children of a REFUSED entry adopted), W02 and W08 (unanchored regexps), W03 (a helper outcome for an unrequested pid accepted), M12 is equivalent.

Ownership by recorded identity (pid + creation time) holds, but a process whose parent id points INTO the owned tree and whose creation time is not earlier than that parent's is ADOPTED and killed at termination (ppid is not authenticated; same-user code can choose it). The README limits say only that a forged id pointing elsewhere is never owned: state the dangerous direction and never adopt the children of a refused entry.

Helper text embedded in a JS string (the C# here-string of windows.cjs) is invisible to Node coverage: the worker's four real-process tests kill only 3 of 7 helper-text mutants (C01 identity compare removed, C04 TERMINATE right dropped, C06 compare with >); C02 (killed returned without waiting for the process object) and C03 (every OpenProcess failure reported as gone, so a DENIED handle reads as gone) survive. Add real bounded fixtures that kill them before trusting a `terminated` for Edge children.

Disclosure from the review (F13): six long-lived msedge renderer processes of the owner's interactive Edge (ppid 19528, ages 40 minutes to 40 hours) vanished within one 10-minute window while the reviewer's only real kill-adapter calls named an impossible pid; most likely Edge's own tab discarding, not U004. Reviews of U005 and U006 that run real kills should record a before and after table of FOREIGN processes and compare, and run real-process probes only against throwaway fixtures started by the reviewer.

HELD: the goal (771 named and 3000 seeded model-checked cases in a separate process: no hub session and no answer behind any refusal, every refused connection closed; the pre-fix control fails 321 of 771), 180/180 in 18 files (slowest 31.8 s), coverage server 99.42/96.32/95.24 framing 100/98.55/100 stream 100/98.04/100 conversation 100/100/96.55 page 100/100/100, Edge 8 checks, RED replay 48 of 55 fail on assertions, the addendum chain 35/35. F1 (REGRESSION, resource exhaustion): requests the fix DROPS (never answered, never destroyed) produce no output, and Node pauses a pipelining socket only when the output queued behind an unfinished answer reaches the write high-water mark, so after a refusal or while /transcript.json is in flight Node keeps parsing and retaining one IncomingMessage and one ServerResponse per pipelined request: a child with --max-old-space-size=48, 3 sockets each sending one GET /transcript.json (or GET /nope, or a held transcript) then 50 blocks of 64 KB of GET /scope.json (about 50k requests per socket) dies with exit 134 in 9 of 9 runs (the pre-U040 bytes survived 7 of 7, peak heap 18-31 MB); with the default heap 92-227 MB against 20-31 MB and a stall of the event loop of more than 5 s. Verified fix direction: count the requests dropped on a marked connection (a WeakMap next to closing) and destroy the socket after 16 (the earlier answers of [G][R][M] are still delivered); a bare request.socket.pause() at the mark sites is NOT enough. m1: one write of GET /scope.json with Expect: 100-continue then a valid upgrade creates a hub session after an answer that says Connection: close (checkContinue goes through handle(), which answers without 100 Continue; Node forces Connection: close but closing is not marked): mark the connection when the Expect header is present. m2 the upgrade listener answers with a raw socket.write while Node still holds earlier answers ([G][G][refused upgrade] loses the second answer; identical on the parent); m3 and m4 the documented limits are acceptable; m5 no flood test and no mutant removes a bound; m6 edits of the informational fields of evidence-index-addendum-1.json are undetected (its raw hash is not pinned inside the repository); m7 identifiers in 8 gzip transcripts and 4 manifests. See orders/R5-U040.md.

A dropped pipelined request must be ANSWERED or the SOCKET STOPPED. Node pauses only on queued output; a drop writes none. Keep a per-marked-connection budget (WeakMap), destroy the 17th; bare socket.pause() still died at 3 sockets.

F24 flood probe: send the first request AND the first 64 KB block in ONE write, else a refusal is flushed and the socket closed before the flood arrives and event counts turn non-deterministic. Use a child with --max-old-space-size=48.

A clock-based quiet window (exchange 400 ms) failed under load and keepAliveTimeout is 1 s: use quietMs 3000 for deterministic pipelines and end them with a final Connection: close request. Two loops each failed 1 of 20 before that.
